patch_description: The current Steiner-tree program already achieves the lowest cost (759.09). The recommendation says to try destination-ordering: sort destinations by ascending true Dijkstra cost from src so cheap central paths form the backbone first, then far destinations attach onto the shared tree. I keep the incremental greedy Steiner tree construction (multi-source Dijkstra from tree nodes), but seed the attachment order by ascending single-source Dijkstra distance. I also build the tree once and reuse it across all partitions (the tree per partition is identical since the graph doesn't change), reducing runtime. All sanitization, path-reconstruction guards, and append logic are preserved.
